Rich Tree View - Items

Source: vignettes/rich-tree-view-items.Rmd
rich-tree-view-items.Rmd

Original MUI X documentation: Rich Tree View - Items. The examples of this page are written for R.

library(muiTreeView)
library(htmltools)

The examples of this page use a selection of the functions of the muiMaterial, muiCharts and reactRouter packages, grouped by package and topic:

to_id <- function(x) gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "-", tolower(x))

fns <- rbind(
  data.frame(package = "muiMaterial", group = "Layout", fn = c("Box", "Stack", "Grid")),
  data.frame(package = "muiMaterial", group = "Inputs", fn = c("Button", "TextField", "Slider", "Switch")),
  data.frame(package = "muiMaterial", group = "Navigation", fn = c("Link", "Tabs", "Drawer")),
  data.frame(package = "muiMaterial", group = "Surfaces", fn = c("AppBar", "Toolbar", "Card")),
  data.frame(package = "muiCharts", group = "Charts", fn = c("BarChart", "LineChart", "PieChart", "Gauge")),
  data.frame(package = "muiCharts", group = "Building blocks", fn = c("ChartsContainer", "ChartsXAxis", "ChartsLegend", "Toolbar")),
  data.frame(package = "reactRouter", group = "Routers", fn = c("RouterProvider", "createHashRouter", "createMemoryRouter")),
  data.frame(package = "reactRouter", group = "Routes", fn = c("Route", "Outlet")),
  data.frame(package = "reactRouter", group = "Navigation", fn = c("Link", "NavLink", "Navigate")),
  data.frame(package = "reactRouter", group = "Hooks", fn = c("useParams", "useLoaderData", "useNavigate"))
)
# Stable ids, built from the path: "Navigation", "Link" and "Toolbar" exist in two packages
fns$group_id <- paste(fns$package, to_id(fns$group), sep = "-")
fns$fn_id <- paste0(fns$package, "::", fns$fn)

head(fns)
#>       package  group        fn           group_id                  fn_id
#> 1 muiMaterial Layout       Box muiMaterial-layout       muiMaterial::Box
#> 2 muiMaterial Layout     Stack muiMaterial-layout     muiMaterial::Stack
#> 3 muiMaterial Layout      Grid muiMaterial-layout      muiMaterial::Grid
#> 4 muiMaterial Inputs    Button muiMaterial-inputs    muiMaterial::Button
#> 5 muiMaterial Inputs TextField muiMaterial-inputs muiMaterial::TextField
#> 6 muiMaterial Inputs    Slider muiMaterial-inputs    muiMaterial::Slider

fn_items <- asMuiTree(
  fns,
  levels = c("package", "group", "fn"),
  levels_id = c("package", "group_id", "fn_id")
)

Basic usage

RichTreeView() takes its items as data, with the items argument. Build them from a data frame with asMuiTree(): each column given in levels becomes a level of the tree. MUI docs

RichTreeView(items = fn_items)

See Data frames with asMuiTree() for more options.

Item identifier

Each item must have a unique id. By default, the tree view reads it from the id field, which asMuiTree() creates from the levels_id columns. If your items use another field, tell the tree view where to find it with getItemId. MUI docs

RichTreeView(
  items = list(
    list(
      internalId = "muiCharts",
      label = "muiCharts",
      children = list(
        list(internalId = "muiCharts::BarChart", label = "BarChart"),
        list(internalId = "muiCharts::LineChart", label = "LineChart")
      )
    ),
    list(internalId = "reactRouter", label = "reactRouter")
  ),
  getItemId = JS("(item) => item.internalId")
)

Item label

Each item must have a label, a string. By default, the tree view reads it from the label field. Use getItemLabel to read it from another field, or to build it from several fields. MUI docs

RichTreeView(
  items = list(
    list(
      id = "muiCharts",
      name = "muiCharts",
      children = list(
        list(id = "muiCharts::BarChart", package = "muiCharts", name = "BarChart"),
        list(id = "muiCharts::PieChart", package = "muiCharts", name = "PieChart")
      )
    )
  ),
  defaultExpandedItems = list("muiCharts"),
  getItemLabel = JS("(item) => item.package ? `${item.package}::${item.name}()` : item.name")
)

To render UI elements in the label, see Rich Tree View - Customization, or use SimpleTreeView().

Item children

By default, the tree view reads the children of an item from the children field. Use getItemChildren to read them from another field. MUI docs

RichTreeView(
  items = list(
    list(
      id = "reactRouter",
      label = "reactRouter",
      nodes = list(
        list(id = "reactRouter::Route", label = "Route"),
        list(id = "reactRouter::Outlet", label = "Outlet")
      )
    ),
    list(id = "muiMaterial", label = "muiMaterial")
  ),
  getItemChildren = JS("(item) => item.nodes")
)

Loading state

The loading argument shown in the MUI docs is not part of the Community version bundled with muiTreeView (@mui/x-tree-view 9.0.2). MUI docs

Disabled items

Use isItemDisabled to disable items. It is a JavaScript function that receives an item and returns TRUE to disable it. A convenient pattern in R is to compute the ids to disable from the data frame, and pass them to the function. Here, the React hooks of reactRouter, whose names start with use, are disabled: MUI docs

hooks <- fns$fn_id[startsWith(fns$fn, "use")]
hooks
#> [1] "reactRouter::useParams"     "reactRouter::useLoaderData"
#> [3] "reactRouter::useNavigate"

RichTreeView(
  items = fn_items,
  defaultExpandedItems = list("reactRouter", "reactRouter-hooks"),
  isItemDisabled = JS(sprintf(
    "(item) => %s.includes(item.id)",
    jsonlite::toJSON(hooks)
  ))
)

Focus disabled items

By default, the keyboard navigation skips the disabled items. Use disabledItemsFocusable = TRUE to let them receive the focus. MUI docs

RichTreeView(
  items = fn_items,
  defaultExpandedItems = list("reactRouter", "reactRouter-hooks"),
  disabledItemsFocusable = TRUE,
  isItemDisabled = JS(sprintf(
    "(item) => %s.includes(item.id)",
    jsonlite::toJSON(hooks)
  ))
)

Item height

Use itemHeight to set the height of each item, in pixels. MUI docs

RichTreeView(
  items = fn_items,
  itemHeight = 48,
  defaultExpandedItems = list("muiCharts")
)

DOM structure

By default, the children of an item are rendered inside it (domStructure = "nested"). Use domStructure = "flat" to render all the items as siblings, with an indentation that reflects their depth. MUI docs

RichTreeView(
  items = fn_items,
  domStructure = "flat",
  defaultExpandedItems = list("muiCharts", "muiCharts-charts")
)

Track item clicks

Use onItemClick to know which item was clicked. In Shiny, send the clicked id to the server with onItemClick = setInput("clickedItem", 1). On this page, which runs without a Shiny server, a JS() function writes it below the tree instead. MUI docs

div(
  RichTreeView(
    items = fn_items,
    onItemClick = JS(
      "(event, itemId) => { document.getElementById('rtv-click').textContent = itemId; }"
    )
  ),
  tags$pre("Last clicked item: ", tags$span(id = "rtv-click", "none"))
)
Last clicked item: 
none

See Shiny for complete apps.

Imperative API

The MUI imperative API (apiRef, e.g. to get an item, its parent or its children from JavaScript) relies on a React hook, which is not available from R. In R, you can look up the same information in the data frame. MUI docs
